newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina posts $139 mln trade deficit in March.
newsitem.headline: Argentina posts $139 mln trade deficit in March.

text.p: Argentina posted a trade deficit of $139 million in March, compared with an $87 million surplus in March 1996, the Economy Ministry said Tuesday.
The country had a trade deficit of $785 million in the first quarter, up from a deficit of $248 million in the first three months of 1996, the ministry said.
Exports in the quarter rose to $5.61 billion from $4.74 billion in the January-March 1996 period. Imports, meanwhile, climbed to $6.40 billion from $4.99 billion.
Imports of capital goods in the quarter rose 49 percent from the comparable 1996 period, while imports of consumer goods rose 25 percent and automobiles were up 36 percent.
Exports of primary products rose 53 percent in the quarter while sales abroad of processed farm products fell one percent.

Argentine exports rose 17 percent to fellow Mercosur customs members Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay, rose four percent to North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) countries Mexico, the United States and Canada, and were up 34 percent to ASEAN countries.
Imports were up 22 percent from Mercosur nations, 33 percent from NAFTA and 55 percent from ASEAN.
